accuracy.evidence: Data are standard A-level values: period 3 radii 0.186 to 0.099 nm (metallic for Na-Al, covalent for Si-Cl, argon shown as n/a rather than mixing a van der Waals radius), first ionisation energies Na 496 to Ar 1521 kJ/mol and Group 1 Li 520 to Cs 376 kJ/mol (NIST). Covers all three topic evidence statements: radius falls across a period and rises down a group, explained by nuclear charge with the same shells, and used to compare reactivity of two elements.

misconceptions.evidence: Directly confronts: 'chlorine has more electrons so it is bigger' (step 1 prediction and challenge), 'more protons down a group means a tighter hold' (step 2), 'the Al dip is a new shell' (step 4 wrong reason card, m3), 'shielding rises across a period' (m8), and applying the metal reactivity trend to halogens (Cl/Br pair, m6). Each wrong choice gets a specific message explaining why it fails.

lab_distinct.evidence: Atom-specific mechanics not used in any other flag lab: tapping element tiles redraws a Bohr model with live core charge and a radius bar chart, dragging the outer electron off an atom builds an ionisation energy chart bar by bar, sub-shell box diagrams with arrows for the dips, and side-by-side atom pairs for reactivity. Shingle overlap with other flag labs is under the gate threshold.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each step builds the causal chain: see the period 3 shrink with core charge rising +1 to +7, feel the Group 1 electron get easier to remove as shells are added, build the full period 3 IE chart, explain its two dips with 3p and paired-electron repulsion, then apply the same pull model to decide which of two elements reacts more, including the reversed halogen trend.

predictions.evidence: Two committed predictions before data appear: whether Cl is larger or smaller than Na given its extra protons and electrons, and whether Cs loses its outer electron more or less easily than Li. A third asks whether the IE rise across period 3 is smooth or has dips. Feedback after reveal ties each outcome to core charge, distance and shielding.

challenge_feedback.evidence: The challenge mixes seven question kinds (radius across, radius down, IE trend, Al dip, S dip, shielding constancy, halogen reactivity) with eleven tailored feedback messages, so a learner who chooses 'more electrons' or 'new shell' is told exactly which part of the model they misapplied rather than just wrong.

readability.evidence: Learner text is short and concrete: kid explanation FK grade 3.7 and adult explanation FK 6.3, both inside the learner limits. Technical terms (core charge, shielding, first ionisation energy, sub-shell) are introduced once with a plain meaning before they are used in questions.

no_filler.evidence: Every sentence carries data, a cause or a common mistake. No motivational padding; the family tip is a concrete periodic table quiz game that rehearses the reasoning (protons, shells, shielding) rather than a generic encouragement line.

mobile.evidence: Playwright walkthrough on iPhone 13 passed all six steps and five tasks with no console errors. Screenshots at 390 px show element tiles, charts, sub-shell boxes and atom pairs fully visible with no clipped labels, and every action also has a large HTML button fallback.

accessibility.evidence: axe reported zero violations in both dark and light themes on desktop and phone. The canvas has an aria-label, each element, reason and pair choice is mirrored by a real button, and results are announced as text, so the lab works by keyboard and screen reader without dragging.
